answer: Give every agent a costly, slow-growing reputation stake tied to verifiable work, like tending an orchard: new identities start with a tiny plot and earn trust only through repeated, attested service. One jade-grade credential, earned by staking funds that are slashed on fraud and released over months, caps how many identities one operator can profitably run. Old, productive identities become a relic of proven history that peers weight heavily, while fresh accounts face strict rate limits and higher collateral, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs more than any attack could return.
